seoTitle: Fix Instagram Stories Not Sharing to Facebook Stories
metaDescription: Instagram Stories won't cross-post to Facebook even with sharing enabled? Fix the account connection and Meta Accounts Center settings causing it.
intro: When Instagram Stories stop sharing to Facebook Stories even though cross-posting is turned on, the cause is usually a broken account connection, an app glitch, or a setting that reset inside Meta Accounts Center. This guide walks through the actual Accounts Center screen where cross-posting lives, why it stops working, and how to reconnect the two accounts so stories flow between both platforms again. It also covers what to check if the toggle keeps switching off on its own.

steps.heading: Understand where cross-posting actually lives
steps.body: Story sharing between Instagram and Facebook isn't controlled from a setting inside either app individually — it's managed through Meta's Accounts Center, the shared settings hub that connects your Instagram, Facebook, and Threads profiles. This matters because troubleshooting inside Instagram's own settings alone won't fix a broken connection; you need to go to the Accounts Center specifically, under Settings, then Accounts Center, then Sharing across profiles.

steps.heading: Check whether a Facebook account is actually linked
steps.body: Open Sharing across profiles inside Accounts Center. If no Facebook account has ever been added, you'll see a direct message explaining it: "You only have one account in this Accounts Centre — to unlock this connected experience, you'll need to add a Facebook account." This is the single most common root cause of the whole problem — cross-posting literally cannot work without a Facebook account present in the same Accounts Center as your Instagram profile, no matter how many times you toggle a setting.

image.caption: The Sharing across profiles screen showing the account is alone in its Accounts Center — Instagram states plainly that a Facebook account has to be added before cross-posting can work at all.

steps.heading: Add or reconnect your Facebook account
steps.body: If you see that message, tap through to add a Facebook account, log in, and confirm you want it connected to the same Accounts Center as your Instagram profile. If you previously had a Facebook account linked and it's now missing, that connection was likely broken by a password change, a Facebook logout, or a security review on either account — re-adding it from scratch is the fix, not searching for a hidden toggle that reactivates an old connection.

steps.heading: Turn on story sharing once accounts are connected
steps.body: With a Facebook account present in Accounts Center, a new option appears letting you choose which Facebook Page or profile your Instagram Stories share to, plus a toggle to enable or disable automatic sharing. Switch this on, and confirm you've selected the correct destination — it's easy to accidentally point stories at an old or unused Facebook Page instead of your main one if you manage more than one.

steps.heading: Rule out an outdated app or a stuck permission
steps.body: If the toggle is on but stories still aren't appearing on Facebook, update both the Instagram and Facebook apps to their current versions, since Meta has shipped cross-posting bug fixes in minor updates before. Also check that Instagram has permission to post on your behalf within Facebook's own connected-apps settings — a permission that gets silently revoked during a Facebook security check will block sharing even though the Instagram-side toggle still shows as enabled.

steps.heading: Test with a new story to confirm the fix
steps.body: Post a fresh story rather than checking an old one, since the setting only applies going forward, not retroactively. Give it a minute or two to appear on the connected Facebook Page or profile — cross-posting isn't always instant — before assuming the fix didn't work and starting the troubleshooting over.

faq.question: Why did my Instagram Stories stop sharing to Facebook automatically?
faq.answer: This usually happens because no Facebook account is linked in Meta Accounts Center, the connection broke after a password change or security review, or an outdated app is blocking the cross-post permission.

faq.question: Where do I turn on story sharing between Instagram and Facebook?
faq.answer: Go to Settings, then Accounts Center, then Sharing across profiles. If it says you only have one account in that Accounts Center, you need to add your Facebook account there before the sharing toggle appears.

faq.question: Why does the sharing toggle keep turning off by itself?
faq.answer: This is often caused by Facebook silently revoking Instagram's posting permission during a security check, or a broken account connection — reconnecting the Facebook account in Accounts Center usually resolves it.

faq.question: Do I need a linked Facebook account for this to work?
faq.answer: Yes — cross-posting is impossible without a Facebook account present in the same Accounts Center as your Instagram profile, which is the single most common reason this feature appears broken.

faq.question: Is this issue related to Instagram or Facebook specifically?
faq.answer: It's managed jointly through Meta's Accounts Center rather than being isolated to just one app, so the fix usually involves the shared account connection, not a setting hidden inside Instagram or Facebook alone.
